questions.prompt: What does the derivative of a function measure?
options: How fast the output changes as the input changes
The maximum value of the function
questions.explanation: A derivative is the rate of change of the output with respect to the input.

questions.prompt: What is the derivative of f(g(x))?
questions.explanation: Chain rule: differentiate the outer function at g(x), then multiply by the derivative of the inner function.

questions.prompt: In a neural network layer, what does multiplying the weight matrix by the input vector produce?
options: A new vector of weighted sums
questions.explanation: Each row of the weight matrix produces one weighted sum, giving a new vector.

questions.prompt: What does a loss function measure?
options: How far predictions are from true values
How many layers the network has
questions.explanation: The loss quantifies prediction error; learning tries to make it small.

questions.prompt: In gradient descent, in which direction are the weights moved?
options: In the direction of the gradient
questions.explanation: The gradient points uphill; stepping opposite to it decreases the loss.

questions.prompt: Why do neural networks use activation functions like ReLU?
questions.explanation: Without non-linearity, stacked layers collapse into one linear function.

options: Gradients flow from output to input
Input flows through each layer to produce a prediction
questions.explanation: Forward propagation computes the prediction layer by layer.

questions.prompt: Which mathematical rule does backpropagation apply layer by layer to compute gradients?
questions.explanation: Backprop is repeated application of the chain rule, from the output backwards.
